summary: Five mild weeknight dinners for 2 adults and a 2-year-old, all from one Lidl shop. Adults add chilli at the table.
savers: Tuesday's rice is cooked double, so Wednesday is a 20-minute dinner.
One 1 kg chicken pack covers Tuesday and Friday: freeze half on Tuesday, thaw in the fridge Thursday night.

days.title: Dal bhat with spinach tarkari
days.intro: The cheapest night of the week: lentils, rice and frozen spinach.
ingredients: 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp cumin seeds (or ground cumin)
method: Rinse lentils and simmer in 900 ml water with turmeric for 20 min until soft; whisk smooth.
Meanwhile cook the rice.
Fry cumin seeds in butter 30 seconds, add chopped onion, garlic and ginger, cook 5 min; add tomato and cook 3 min. Pour half of this tadka into the dal.
Add the frozen spinach to the remaining tadka and cook 5–6 min until fairly dry. That's the tarkari.
Serve the toddler's portion, then salt the adults' dal and add chilli or achar.
days.toddler: Dal mixed into rice is an easy spoon food; a small knob of butter on top makes it extra appealing.

days.title: Mild chicken & coconut curry with rice
days.intro: A korma-style curry toddlers usually love. Cook double rice tonight and refrigerate half for Wednesday.
ingredients: 500 g plain chicken breast fillet (half of a 1 kg pack; freeze the rest for Friday)
200 g passata or ½ can chopped tomatoes
2 tsp garam masala (or mild curry powder), 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp ground cumin, 1 tsp ground coriander
Optional: frozen peas or cubed potato to stretch it
method: Cut chicken into small bite-size pieces.
Fry onion in oil 6–8 min until soft and golden; add garlic, ginger and ground spices for 1 min.
Add passata, cook 3 min, then the chicken; stir until no longer pink outside.
Pour in coconut milk and simmer 12–15 min until the chicken is cooked through.
Cook the rice. Spread the spare half on a plate to cool quickly, then refrigerate within an hour.
Serve the toddler's portion before seasoning; adults add salt, chilli and fresh coriander.
days.toddler: Shred a few chicken pieces with a fork for easier chewing.

days.title: Egg fried rice with peas & carrot
days.intro: The quick night. Cold leftover rice from Tuesday fries best.
ingredients: Tuesday's leftover cooked rice (about 900 g cooked)
200 g frozen peas, 1 carrot (or 300 g frozen mixed veg)
2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil (optional)
method: Break up the cold rice with your fingers so there are no clumps.
Beat the eggs; scramble softly in a hot wok or large pan with 1 tbsp oil, then tip out.
Add the rest of the oil, fry diced carrot 3 min, then garlic, white part of spring onion and peas 2 min.
Add the rice and fry on high heat 4–5 min, pressing it against the pan.
Return the eggs and add spring onion greens. Take out the toddler's portion, then add soy sauce and sesame oil for the adults.
days.toddler: Give the toddler's portion just a few drops of soy sauce; regular soy sauce is very salty for a 2-year-old.
days.note: Food safety: only reheat rice that was cooled fast and refrigerated. Use it within 1 day and reheat until piping hot.

days.title: Keema matar with flatbread
days.intro: Spiced chicken mince with peas and potato, scooped up with warm flatbread. The potato stretches 400 g of mince to feed everyone.
ingredients: 200 g passata or ½ can chopped tomatoes
2 tsp garam masala (or mild curry powder), 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp turmeric
2 tbsp natural yoghurt (optional, makes it creamier)
1 pack tortilla wraps or pita breads, or rice
method: Brown the chicken mince in 1 tbsp oil for 5 min, breaking it up finely.
Add onion and cook 5 min, then garlic, ginger and spices for 1 min.
Add potato, passata and 150 ml water. Cover and simmer 15 min until the potato is soft.
Stir in peas for the last 3 min and the yoghurt off the heat.
Warm the flatbreads in a dry pan. Serve the toddler first, then season the rest.
days.toddler: Fine mince with soft potato is easy to chew; roll some into a small wrap for a hand-held dinner.

days.title: Nepali-style chicken chow mein
days.intro: Kathmandu street-style noodles with chicken and plenty of cabbage, using the second half of Tuesday's chicken.
ingredients: 500 g chicken breast fillet, thinly sliced (thawed overnight in the fridge)
3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp ketchup, ½ tsp turmeric or curry powder
method: Mix the chicken with 1 tbsp soy sauce, garlic and ginger; leave 10 min.
Cook the noodles 1 min less than the pack says; drain and toss with a little oil.
Stir-fry the chicken in a hot pan 4–5 min until cooked; tip out.
Stir-fry onion, carrot, pepper and cabbage 4 min, keeping some crunch.
Add noodles, chicken, turmeric, ketchup and the rest of the soy sauce; toss 2 min.
Take out the toddler's portion before the last soy sauce; adults add chilli sauce at the table.
days.toddler: Snip the noodles into short lengths with kitchen scissors.

items.name: Chicken breast fillet, plain (broilerin rintafilee, maustamaton), 1 kg
Butter, if not already at home

pantry: Turmeric, ground cumin or cumin seeds, ground coriander
Garam masala or mild curry powder
tips: Swap protein to price: if boneless chicken thighs are on offer, use them instead of breast.
Extra dal freezes well in small portions for the toddler's lunches.
Spices last for months, so after the first week the pantry cost drops to almost nothing.
Season the pot lightly; a 2-year-old needs far less salt than adults.
Keep chilli flakes or chilli sauce on the table instead of in the pot.
Halve round foods like cherry tomatoes and keep whole spices out of the toddler's bowl.
